note: Coarse, category-level directions of travel as roast development continues - Perturbation's whole answer key. Deliberately categorical (up/down/mixed), not a numeric model: this project does not have per-degree roast-curve data any more than it has the perceptual-distance data behind the wheel's gap widths, and won't invent either. What follows is standard roasting chemistry taught in any Q or SCA roasting course, not original research.
reviewTarget: Needs the same Q-grader pass as the confusable table before v1 - directionally uncontroversial, but nobody with a Q certification has signed off on it yet.

trends.note: This category is the direct byproduct of pyrolysis - by definition, more roasting means more of it, right through to Burnt past second crack.
Maillard browning is the direct source of nutty and cocoa character; it builds steadily as development continues.
Brown spice notes (cinnamon, clove, nutmeg) are Maillard products that build with development, the same reaction driving Roasted and Nutty/Cocoa upward.

Caramelization builds brown-sugar sweetness through most of the roast, but perceived sweetness typically peaks around medium development and is masked by bitterness in dark roasts - net direction depends on where the comparison sits, so this is not a clean up or down.

Delicate fruit-forward aromatics and the organic acids that carry them are among the first casualties of continued roasting; the fruit brightness that defines a light roast fades toward brown-sugar and roast character as development continues.

Chlorogenic acids degrade steadily through the roast, which is the main reason perceived acidity falls as roast advances - true of the clean acids and of the fermented/winey notes, which fade under caramelization too.
Grassy, vegetal notes are a signature of under-development; they burn off early in the roast and are essentially gone by the time development is well underway.
The most volatile aromatics in the cup, and the first lost to heat; floral character is a light-roast signature that fades fastest of all.

This category bundles green-coffee defects (chemical, papery/musty) that trace to handling before the roast, not to the roast itself - continued roasting neither reliably creates nor removes them, so there is no clean roast-direction claim to make here.
